title: INPUT_nscf must stay symmetry = -1 whenever the LibRPA symmetry switches are on (validators must check it, not only INPUT_scf)
symptom: A controlled-execution admission layer accepted cases with `INPUT_scf symmetry=1`, LibRPA symmetry switches on, but `INPUT_nscf symmetry=1` - a configuration that violates the full-k-point NSCF/band preprocessing flow and should never reach execution.
root_cause: The materializer/validator (oml_mcp materializer.py:70) parsed INPUT_nscf but only checked spin and resource directories, and the symmetry alignment check used only INPUT_scf, so an inconsistent NSCF symmetry setting passed admission.
minimal_fix: In the standard symmetry lane keep `INPUT_scf` at `symmetry = 1` (to generate the IBZ sidecars) while `INPUT_nscf`/`INPUT` stay at `symmetry = -1` (full k points for bands/PyATB), and extend the admission validator to require `symmetry = -1` in INPUT_nscf and to check symmetry consistency across INPUT_scf, INPUT_nscf and librpa.in.
validation: Static preflight over all three files: fail with a clear message when INPUT_nscf has symmetry != -1 while LibRPA symmetry flags are enabled; confirm the accepted reference cases use INPUT_scf symmetry=1 / INPUT_nscf symmetry=-1 (as in the SiC sg15 df sym+shrink case) and produce sidecars irreducible_sector.txt plus symrot_*.txt.
avoid: Do not validate symmetry from INPUT_scf alone, and do not 'unify' symmetry across SCF/NSCF by setting both to 1 - that removes the full-k NSCF products the band/head-wing steps need.
